issues.explanation: The change ships no tests at all for three new actions, the policy, the model, the migration or the two newly authorized call paths, although conventions.md makes a test per feature and per authorization/validation failure path mandatory.

All four abilities depend on `User::membershipFor()`, which is not part of this diff; if that helper does not already exist (the removed code in Ticket::call queried EntityMembership inline), every authorization check fails at runtime, so its existence must be verified.

Name length is checked with byte-based `strlen()`, so a valid multibyte name under 255 characters (e.g. 100 accented/emoji characters) is wrongly rejected; `Str::length()`/`mb_strlen()` would match the 1-255 character rule.
An explicit empty slug slugifies to an empty string and is stored, leaving a queue with no usable slug; an empty result should be a ValidationException.

`isUniqueViolation()` returns true for any SQLSTATE 23000, so an unrelated integrity failure (e.g. a bad entity_id or membership FK) is reported as 'The slug has already been taken' instead of surfacing the real error.
The unique-violation detection helper is duplicated verbatim from CreateQueue (app/Actions/CreateQueue.php:53-63); it should live in one place instead of two similar copies.

The afterMaking hook is convoluted and contains unreachable branches (lines 48-53 and 548-552 test a null that the enclosing branch already excluded), and when only a queue_id is given and that queue is missing it can create a membership in a different entity, breaking the 'same entity' requirement.
The change deletes the only `EntityMembership::query()` usage in the model, but the diff shows no removal of the corresponding import, which Pint's unused-import rule will reject.
Only the summary line is updated; the queue_access table description elsewhere in the file is not adjusted to say it is now migrated rather than a proposal.

review.summary: The change implements the full domain/authorization slice as specified — three actions, the QueueAccess model/migration/factory, the QueuePermission enum, the auto-discovered QueuePolicy and `call` enforcement in both CallNextTicket and Ticket::call() — with authorization, validation and docs in place. It is not approvable as is because it ships no tests whatsoever, and the policy's reliance on an unshown `User::membershipFor()` helper needs verification; smaller issues are byte-based name length, empty slugs, over-broad unique-violation detection, and a needlessly convoluted factory.
